title: Package Publishing: npm, PyPI, Maven & crates.io
description: Cross-ecosystem package publishing reference covering versioning, compatibility, artifact contents, metadata, licenses, changelogs, credentials, trusted publishing, provenance, npm, PyPI, Maven Central, crates.io, CI release workflows, yanking/deprecation, incident response, and maintainer continuity.

subtopics.title: Versions, Compatibility & Release Policy
subtopics.description: Define what public API means for the ecosystem, use semantic versioning where applicable, document supported runtimes/platforms, and review transitive compatibility before changing a version.

codeBlocks.code:
Patch: compatible fixes/security updates
Minor: backward-compatible capabilities (pre-1.0 ecosystem rules may differ)
Major: intentionally breaking public contract
Pre-release: explicit unstable identifier; dependency resolution rules vary
Release policy: support window, deprecation period, security channel, cadence

callouts.title: SemVer Does Not Define Your Public API
callouts.text: Document whether types, CLI flags, config, wire formats, generated code, behavior, errors, performance, or transitive dependencies are compatibility commitments.

subtopics.title: Artifact Contents, Metadata & Licenses
subtopics.description: Inspect the exact archive before upload. Include required runtime files, declarations/sources, README, license, repository, authorship, supported versions, and exclude secrets, tests, fixtures, build caches, and private configuration.

codeBlocks.code:
Inspect archive listing and unpack it into an empty directory
Install/build/test only from the packed artifact
Verify entry points, generated files, type metadata, licenses, notices
Scan secrets, personal paths, credentials, source maps and oversized assets
Confirm package name/namespace/version/registry before upload

callouts.title: Git Contents and Package Contents Differ
callouts.text: Registry include/exclude rules vary. Always inspect the produced artifact; .gitignore alone is not a universal publishing boundary.

subtopics.title: Trusted Publishing, Provenance & CI Identity
subtopics.description: Prefer registry-supported trusted publishing with short-lived workload identity over stored long-lived tokens. Pin release workflows and actions, restrict environments, and generate provenance where supported.

codeBlocks.code:
Protected tag/release event → trusted CI workflow
→ verify commit/tag and clean source
→ build/test/package in isolated environment
→ authenticate with OIDC/trusted publisher
→ publish immutable version + provenance/signatures
→ verify registry artifact and create release notes

callouts.title: Release CI Is a Production System
callouts.text: Protect workflow changes, environments, tags, maintainers, third-party actions/plugins, and registry ownership. Require review and monitor unexpected releases.

subtopics.title: npm package.json, Exports & Packing
subtopics.description: Define package name/version, files, entry points, ESM/CommonJS policy, types, engines, peer dependencies, side effects, license, and publish configuration. Test the tarball as a consumer.

codeBlocks.code:
npm pack --dry-run
npm pack
npm install ./example-widgets-1.2.0.tgz
npm publish --access public

callouts.title: Lifecycle Scripts Run in Sensitive Contexts
callouts.text: prepack/prepare/prepublishOnly can mutate artifacts or execute dependencies. Keep them deterministic, review output, and avoid downloading unverified tools at release time.

subtopics.title: npm Scopes, Dist-Tags, Staging & Deprecation
subtopics.description: Scopes provide namespaces; dist-tags such as latest/next select install channels independently of version ordering. Use staged/trusted publishing where available and deprecate bad releases with guidance.

codeBlocks.code:
npm publish --tag next --access public
npm dist-tag add @example/widgets@2.0.0 latest
npm deprecate @example/widgets@1.2.3 "Security issue; upgrade to >=1.2.4"
npm owner ls @example/widgets

callouts.title: Unpublish Is Restricted and Disruptive
callouts.text: Treat published versions as immutable. If a secret is included, revoke it immediately; removing or deprecating a package does not erase downloaded artifacts or logs.

subtopics.title: PyPI pyproject.toml, Wheels & sdists
subtopics.description: Declare build backend and project metadata in pyproject.toml. Build both sdist and appropriate wheels, inspect them, and test installation in clean supported environments.

codeBlocks.code:
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "example-widgets"
version = "1.2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = []

python -m build
python -m twine check dist/*
python -m pip install --no-index --find-links dist example-widgets

callouts.title: Wheel Compatibility Tags Matter
callouts.text: Pure Python and compiled-extension wheels have different platform/ABI requirements. Build with maintained tooling and test every claimed interpreter/platform combination.

subtopics.title: PyPI Trusted Publishing, TestPyPI & Uploads
subtopics.description: Configure a PyPI Trusted Publisher for the exact repository/workflow/environment where possible. Use TestPyPI for workflow rehearsal but still test final artifacts locally because dependency availability differs.

codeBlocks.code:
python -m twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*
# Preferred production CI: trusted publisher obtains short-lived identity
# Verify https://pypi.org/project/<distribution>/<version>/ after publish

callouts.title: Distribution and Import Names Can Differ
callouts.text: Document both, check name ownership and typo-squatting risk, and verify the installed import/API from the built wheel—not the repository checkout.

subtopics.title: Maven Coordinates, POM & Release Artifacts
subtopics.description: Coordinates are groupId:artifactId:version. Central releases need complete POM metadata and typically binary, sources, Javadoc, checksums, and signatures according to current portal requirements.

callouts.title: Released Coordinates Are Immutable
callouts.text: Do not reuse a version. Publish a corrected version, communicate the defect, and preserve reproducible source/tag relationships.

subtopics.title: Maven Central Portal Publishing
subtopics.description: Verify namespace ownership, configure the current Central publishing plugin or portal workflow, keep credentials out of the POM, validate the deployment bundle, and publish only after checks pass.

codeBlocks.code:
./mvnw -DskipTests=false verify
./mvnw deploy
# Inspect Central Portal deployment validation/state
# Verify POM, module metadata, sources, Javadoc, signatures and checksums

callouts.title: Snapshot and Release Repositories Differ
callouts.text: Snapshots are mutable development artifacts under snapshot semantics; Central releases are immutable. Ensure CI routes and credentials to the intended destination.

subtopics.title: Cargo.toml & Crate Packaging
subtopics.description: Provide license, description, repository, README, keywords/categories, Rust edition and rust-version where appropriate. Use include/exclude carefully and inspect the crate archive.

codeBlocks.code:
[package]
name = "example-widgets"
version = "1.2.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.85"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://example.com/widgets"
readme = "README.md"

cargo package --list
cargo package
cargo publish --dry-run

callouts.title: Test the Minimum Supported Rust Version
callouts.text: A rust-version declaration is a compatibility promise. Dependencies and enabled features must also resolve and compile under that toolchain.

subtopics.title: crates.io Publish, Owners & Yank
subtopics.description: Publish after dry-run from a clean tagged commit, use scoped registry tokens or trusted mechanisms where supported, maintain multiple owners, and yank only to prevent new resolution of a broken release.

codeBlocks.code:
cargo publish --dry-run
cargo publish
cargo owner --list
cargo yank --version 1.2.3
cargo yank --version 1.2.3 --undo

callouts.title: Yanking Does Not Delete a Crate
callouts.text: Existing lockfiles can continue using it and the archive remains. Revoke leaked secrets immediately and publish a fixed version with an advisory.

subtopics.title: Monorepos, Dependency Order & Coordinated Releases
subtopics.description: Build a package dependency graph, decide fixed versus independent versioning, publish dependencies before consumers, and wait for registry visibility before downstream publication.

codeBlocks.code:
Graph: core → adapters → framework integration → examples
Plan: changed public APIs → affected dependents → version bumps
Preflight: clean artifact tests for every package
Publish: topological order; verify registry/index availability
Failure: stop, record published subset, resume safely without reusing versions

callouts.title: Publishing Is Not Atomic Across Registries or Packages
callouts.text: Design resumable release state and avoid consumers depending on versions not yet visible. Never overwrite or silently rebuild an already published version.

subtopics.title: Post-Publish Verification & Incident Response
subtopics.description: Install from the public registry into clean environments, verify checksums/provenance/metadata, exercise a minimal consumer, monitor reports, and prepare an advisory/deprecation/yank/fix-forward workflow.

codeBlocks.code:
Verify exact version and registry URL
Download/install without workspace/source fallback
Run import/compile/basic-use smoke tests
Inspect published metadata, dependencies, signatures/provenance
If compromised: revoke credentials → notify registry/security → advisory
→ deprecate/yank where useful → publish fix → communicate migration

callouts.title: A Secret in an Artifact Is Already Compromised
callouts.text: Deletion, yank, or unpublish cannot recall mirrors, caches, downloads, logs, or forks. Revoke and rotate first, then handle registry cleanup.

subtopics.title: Maintainer Continuity & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Avoid single-person ownership, require strong authentication, document release/recovery, monitor ownership changes, and periodically test release from a clean trusted environment.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Define compatibility, inspect/test packed artifacts, use trusted short-lived publishing, protect release workflows/tags, generate provenance, keep multiple maintainers, never reuse versions, verify public installs, monitor unexpected releases, and rehearse credential compromise and fix-forward.
